content.text:
The drawing is a benzene ring with four substituents.

Ring atoms, going around the ring:
- C1 carries the nitrile (C≡N).
- C2, adjacent to C1, carries an OH (top).
- C3, next to C2, carries NO2 (upper left).
- C4 and C5 are plain CH positions along the bottom left and bottom.
- C6, adjacent to C1 on the other side, carries an OH (bottom right).

So the molecule is 2,6-dihydroxy-3-nitrobenzonitrile.

SMILES, written ring-first from the nitrile carbon: N#Cc1c(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1O

Check: c1 (the C–CN carbon), then c(O) (C2), then c(NO2) (C3), then c and c (C4 and C5), then c1O (C6 with OH). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1c(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1O
